mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months indicates an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods when FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.5 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates a dual shock of monetary tightening and economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE increase by more than 0.2 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In the late phase of an economic expansion, a decline in housing starts below 1400 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand and potential recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST falls below 1400 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate over the past three months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110.0 (index 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when INDPRO falls below 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and industrial production signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings growth and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods when both HOUST and INDPRO decline by more than 2% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase, a sustained increase in non-farm payrolls above 200 thousand jobs per month signals strong employment growth, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in labor market recovery periods when PAYEMS exceeds 200 thousand jobs per month.
